name: Roy Chi Ping Chung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Global (2022); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Roy Chi Ping Chung cofounded Techtronic Industries with fellow billionaire Horst Julius Pudwill in 1985.
He debuted as a billionaire in 2021 when shares in Techtronic, a maker of power equipment and floor-care cleaning products, rose amid consumer demand.
The company makes cordless powered products for Milwaukee Tool, Ryobi DIY power equipment and the iconic Hoover brand.
He retired as group vice chairman and executive director of Techtronic in 2011, and has since been a non-executive director.

name: Sam Tarascio
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Sam Tarascio owns a portfolio of real estate across Melbourne, including a business park, two distribution sites, a large shopping mall and a market.
Tarascio, who emigrated from Italy in the 1950s, also owns several inner-city apartment developments.
He started out in property development in the 1960s by building a warehouse for German pharmaceutical company Hoechst, where he had worked in sales.
That led him to establish logistics and industrial-development business Salta Properties, now run by his son Sam.
Sam Tarascio, founder of Salta Properties, will transition from his role as founding director to non-executive founding director, effective 1 January 2026.
forbes_facts: Tarascio imported an olive press in 2014 for his Taralinga Estate on the Mornington Peninsula, near Melbourne.
His Taralinga Estate olive oil has won two gold medals at the New York International World Olive Oil Competition.

name: Marco Squinzi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Marco Squinzi is the co-CEO and part-owner of MAPEI, a manufacturer of chemical products used in construction based in Milan, Italy.
He and his sister Veronica became co-CEOs in July 2019, three months before the death of their father Giorgio, who took over the company in 1984.
MAPEI was founded by Giorgio's father, Rodolfo, in 1937; its products have been used to restore the Coliseum in Rome and in the Panama City metro.
Marco shares ownership of MAPEI with Veronica and his cousin Simona Giorgetta, who owns the largest stake in the company.
Together with his sister and his cousin, he also owns Italian soccer team Sassuolo Calcio, which Giorgio acquired in 2003.

name: Cao Ji
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Cao Ji chairs Zhejiang Hangke Technology, a supplier to the lithium battery industry.
Hangke went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Cao has more than a 60% stake in Hangke with his son Cao Zheng, a company director.
Hangke is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

name: Pedro Grendene Bartelle
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Grendene Bartelle cofounded his eponymous company Grendene, one of the world's largest sandal manufacturers, with his twin brother Alexandre.
He is vice chairman of the board of directors at Grendene and owns just under 14% of the Sao Paulo-listed company.
Grendene Bartelle invests in other companies such as footwear maker Vulcabras, where he serves as chairman and holds a 50% stake.
His son Pedro runs Vulcabras as its CEO.
forbes_facts: Grendene Bartelle is married to Tania Bulhoes, a Brazilian entrepreneur who owns Tania Bulhoes Perfumes Ltda., a well known retailer of perfumes, creams and soaps.

name: Joao Alves de Queiroz Filho
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2010-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Consumer goods tycoon Joao Alvez de Queiroz Filho, known as Junior, cofounded Arisco, a cleaning products business, with his father in 1969.
In 2000, he founded Hypermarcas, a Brazilian version of Unilever selling food, drugs, cleaning supplies, and beauty and personal hygiene products.
Hypermarcas SA went public in 2008. It grew through acquisitions, new product launches and publicity with celebrities.
Coty, founded in Paris in 1904, purchased the personal care and consumer goods units of Hypermarcas for a reported $1 billion in 2016.
In December 2017, the company changed its legal name to Hypera Pharma; it makes prescription as well as non-prescription drugs.

name: Herald Chen
sec_insider_companies: AppLovin Corp (APP) - Director; GoDaddy Inc. (GDDY) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Herald Chen is a former president and chief financial officer of AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin.
Chen became a billionaire thanks to stock options he was awarded when he joined the Palo Alto, California-based company in 2019.
As AppLovin's CFO, Chen helped the company prepare for its 2021 initial public offering on the Nasdaq.
In 2024, Chen transitioned into a new role as advisor to AppLovin's billionaire cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi, while remaining on the company's board.
Chen previously led KKR's technology, media and telecom division for 12 years, overseeing the private equity firm's investments in AppLovin, WebMD, Eastman Kodak and more.
